title: Spain Break Australia's World Record With 21 Consecutive T20I Wins
excerpt: The European associate nation has surpassed Australia's mark for the most consecutive wins in men's international cricket, with a streak built across three years of bilateral series and ICC qualifiers.
body:
• Spain have won 21 consecutive men's T20I matches, breaking Australia's long-standing record for the most consecutive wins in men's international cricket.
  • The streak, which began in November 2022, includes bilateral series whitewashes and unbeaten runs across multiple ICC European qualifiers.
  • Head coach Corey Rutgers has transformed Spain from associate-level minnows into record-breakers, lifting the team to 29th in the ICC T20I rankings.
  • Players of South Asian heritage — including Muhammad Atif, Yasir Ali, and Hamza Saleem Dar — have been central to Spain's rise, reflecting how diaspora communities drive cricket's global growth.

Spain have rewritten cricket's record books. With 21 consecutive victories in men's T20 Internationals, achieved during the ongoing ICC Men's T20 World Cup Europe Sub Regional Qualifier C, the European associate nation has surpassed Australia's long-held record for the most consecutive wins in men's international cricket.

It is a staggering achievement for a country better known for football — and a team that was barely a blip on cricket's radar four years ago.

Three Years of Dominance

The streak began in November 2022, shortly after Spain's last defeat to Italy. Since then, the team has gone on an extraordinary run across bilateral series and ICC qualifying tournaments.

Spain whitewashed the Isle of Man (four wins), Jersey (two), and Croatia (five) in bilateral series before carrying the momentum into successive ICC European pathway qualifiers, beating Cyprus, Czech Republic, Greece, Finland, and Denmark along the way. They first broke Malaysia and Bermuda's record of 13 consecutive men's T20I wins, then surpassed Nigeria's 16-match unbeaten run, and eventually overtook Thailand Women's mark of 17 consecutive T20I victories — the previous all-format record.

Their continued dominance at the 2026 Europe Sub Regional Qualifier C pushed the tally to 21, past Australia's all-time mark in men's international cricket.

"We obviously don't play for records but this does feel special for the group. It has been a transformative few years in Spain, and a lot of credit goes to the players who sacrifice a lot of their time to play for España."

— Corey Rutgers, Spain Head Coach

The Rutgers Revolution

The transformation is the work of head coach Corey Rutgers and assistant Alastair Priddle. Under their stewardship, Spain have climbed from the lower rungs of associate cricket to 29th in the ICC T20I rankings and now hold the best win-loss ratio of any nation in T20I ranking matches, with 35 wins from 43 games.

Spain also hold a Guinness World Record from their bilateral series against the Isle of Man, when they bowled the Manx side out for just 10 runs and chased the target in two legal deliveries — the most lopsided result in T20I history.

South Asian Players Power Spain's Rise

Spain's cricket revolution has been built in part by players of South Asian descent, a pattern mirrored across European cricket. Muhammad Atif, a left-arm seamer, has been one of the squad's most consistent wicket-takers throughout the streak. Yasir Ali delivered match-winning figures of 3/12 in the record-setting win over Greece. All-rounder Hamza Saleem Dar has contributed with both bat and ball across formats.

"We are so proud of our group. We have worked really hard in the last two years — there are so many sacrifices from the boys, and of course we have the best coaching staff as well."

— Muhammad Atif, Spain Cricketer

Their presence reflects how diaspora communities — particularly from South Asia — have driven cricket's growth in non-traditional nations across Europe. For Indian cricket fans, the record carries a particular resonance: India and Afghanistan hold the full-member record at just 12 consecutive T20I wins. Spain, ranked over 60 places below India, have nearly doubled that mark.

Record Stands Despite Qualifier Hurdles

Spain's winning run has not guaranteed smooth tournament progression. A rain-enforced abandonment earlier in the 2026 qualifier complicated their path to the European Regional final, with net run rate tiebreakers potentially working against them. But the record stands regardless of how the tournament plays out.

All-rounder Lorne Burns captured the squad's mood: "Holding the record for most consecutive wins is a great honour and team achievement. It's a testament to where Spanish cricket is and where we are going, and we are all excited for what the future holds."

With cricket set for its Olympic debut and the sport actively expanding into new markets, Spain's streak — built by committed amateurs who balance day jobs with international cricket — is proof that the game's future extends well beyond its traditional powerhouses.
